33.t: Meeting his wife, his daughter and his wife as band leader's partner in Biloxi
33.s: He recalls meeting his wife at 14, her illnesses, his daughter and granddaughter, and her poise at Biloxi dances.
33.ch: Early career, theaters and Cobb's Tea Room
33.q: Yeah. Well, she's... I'm the only man she ever knew. I met her when she was 14. Her mother wouldn't let me take her out. And when I did take her out, I had to take her sister. And everybody wanted to know whether I was calling her or her sister, because they were equally beautiful. And I'll say she…

283.t: Not an arranger; women, horses and three marriages
283.s: He wishes he had learned to arrange, talks of women, cars and horses, and says he was married three times, the last for 28 years.
283.q: One guy used to make an arrangement and then he'd get a couple of guys to copy it. It'd take a long time for it. 10, 12 musicians, you know, to copy the whole thing. You never did the arrangers to yourself? No, I wish I knew how to arrange. Gee. That's one thing I wanted to do, no kidding. But…

887.t: Women in the tribes and costume sewing
887.s: Some tribes have queens, others exclude women; wives and friends help sew costumes over nine months.
887.q: Wives usually work on the costume And many of their friends are willing to work on the costume Which is, to me, very important The fellow will do his sewing He'll have a good friend of his helping him

199.t: Marriage in 1946 and his wife's stroke
199.s: They married in 1946 on his leave, celebrated 50 years, and she had a diabetic stroke in 1980 and needs constant care.
199.ch: Growing up in the Thirteenth Ward
199.q: Yeah, when I went in the service. When I came on my leave, man, we hooked up. That's what I'm saying. We are the 15 of this.

110.s: Rowe notes Mel Torme's summer Christmas song and Iola's role as partner; Brubeck says she usually likes everything but disliked this morning's piece.
110.q: Yeah. Except this morning when she didn’t like my new piece. Because she usually likes everything you know and will give me suggestions. But she said, “don’t let anybody sing that, that’s too sad.”

336.s: He is married to singer Madeline Eastman.
336.q: I’m going to milk it, believe me. You know I’m married to a musician, I’m married to a singer. I don’t know if you knew that, Madeline Eastman, a real good singer. And that works good. We are not the typical husband-wife work together all the time you know. We do but we don’t and it works fine. We…

790.t: Wife Daniella and Uncle Lionel Batiste's funeral
790.s: Player met his wife Daniella in Switzerland; her photos of Lionel Batiste's second line funeral outside their house.
790.q: The gumbo, exactly. You just take it and mix it all up and make something new, and that’s how we get where we are. But it’s very interesting. And I just say to everybody, come to New Orleans. Come to New Orleans and experience it. My wife, Daniella, I met her in Switzerland, and it’s like — you…

61.t: Falling for Anahid, the only girl he proposed to
61.s: He calls marrying violinist Anahid the luckiest thing, and says she taught him classical music.
61.q: Oh yeah, the luckiest thing that ever happened to me, because she’s the most marvelous person I’ve ever known, in addition to being a magnificent musician and a magnificent wife. She’s even a magnificent cook. The fact that I was familiar with the general idea of certain phases of contemporary…

527.t: Farmer's marriages and his first son's death
527.s: First marriage to a South American woman with son Arthur Jr., a second to a cousin, and then his wife in Vienna who died in 1992.
527.q: No, I had met my wife because she was working for the Central Sparkasse. When I started living there, we were living together, then she became pregnant, that’s when we got married.

135.t: Kenny Clarke after leaving: Annie Ross and the son
135.s: Heath recalls Kenny going back to Paris, his marriage to Annie Ross, their son Liaquat, and Carmen McRae.
135.q: Yeah, he wrote all his drum parts, and that is what Kenny didn’t wanna do. Kenny went back to Paris. He wanted to go back to Paris anyhow. He didn’t stay over here very long. At that time, he was married to Annie Ross, and they had a son that they brought back over here.

137.s: After that last big tour he married, has had three or four wives, and ended up raising the children himself.
137.ch: Long Island years and Battle's estate
137.q: No, I've had three or four wives. (Laughter.) I didn't stay with them long. Yeah, married right after I come off of that tour.

231.t: She marries another; old friends and his mother's advice
231.s: He tells of calling the girl, learning she married the visitor, still sending her cards, and his mother's advice.
231.ch: Solo years, marriages and the Canadian party
231.q: don't know he's the guy that's going to marry her, I don't know he's the guy. This is the guy that's going to marry her that I'm talking to.
